transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess the main thing is… I have a hard time sitting still. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it feels like there’s a little motor running under my skin when I’m supposed to stay put, like during staff meetings or church event briefings. I’ll start shifting around, or I’ll stand up, or find some reason to step out or move around. I’m not trying to be disruptive or anything—it’s just uncomfortable to sit there.
Do you find it hard to sit still only during staff meetings or church events, or does this happen in other situations too, like at home or in social gatherings?

It’s mostly when I’m expected to just sit still, like those staff meetings or the church briefings I mentioned. I don’t mean to make a big thing of it, but it’s like this motor humming under my skin, and before I know it I’m shifting around, standing up, or looking for some acceptable reason to move. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any other situations where you have trouble focusing, feel impulsive, or struggle with staying on task, like at work or in conversations?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make myself sound rude, because I’m really not trying to be. But sometimes when my supervisor is giving me instructions, or one of the church staff is explaining something, I’ll jump in before they’re finished. Like I think I already know where they’re going with it, so I answer or finish the thought, and then… sometimes I’m wrong and they have to correct me.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I don’t mean to cut people off. I’m just trying to be helpful or show I’m following along, if that makes sense.
Do you also find yourself shifting or needing to move when you're in other situations that require sitting still, like watching TV at home or working at your desk alone?

I guess it’s really the sitting-still part, wherever that is. I notice it most in staff meetings or church event briefings because I’m supposed to look attentive, you know? I’ll start shifting in my chair, or I’ll feel like I need to stand up, or I’ll think of some excuse to go move around.

It’s not that I’m trying to avoid anything… it just feels like there’s this motor humming under my skin when I’m expected to stay put. Does that answer what you mean?

Do you also feel this need to move or shift around in other places, like when you’re alone at home, watching TV, or reading, or is it mostly only when you’re in meetings or group settings where you’re expected to stay still?

Mostly when there’s that expectation that I’m supposed to sit still and look settled, if that makes sense. Like staff meetings or church event briefings are where I really notice it.

I don’t want to overstate it, but it feels like there’s this motor kind of humming under my skin, and then I’m shifting around, or I end up standing, or I look for some excuse to move. It’s not me trying to be disruptive or anything… I just have a hard time staying put in those moments.
Do you ever feel this same need to move or shift around when you’re in other situations that aren’t formal meetings—like when you’re at home alone, talking with friends, or trying to relax?

I mean… maybe some, but I notice it most when I’m supposed to be sitting still and looking attentive, like in those staff meetings or church briefings.

At home or with friends, it’s not as obvious to me, or maybe I don’t feel as self-conscious about it. But when there’s that expectation to stay put, it’s like that motor humming under my skin starts up, and I’m shifting around or wanting to stand, or looking for a reason to move. I hope that’s answering what you’re asking.

Can you think of any time when you felt that same need to move or shift around when you weren’t in a meeting or a church event—like when you’re at home alone, talking with friends, or trying to relax?

I’m trying to think of a good example… I don’t know that I notice it as much when I’m just relaxing, honestly.

The clearest times are still when I’m supposed to sit still and look like I’m paying attention—staff meetings, church event briefings, things like that. Then it’s like I’ve got this motor humming under my skin, and I start shifting around, or I want to stand up, or I’ll find some little excuse to move.

So… maybe it happens other times too, but those are the ones I can really point to. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever noticed this same feeling of needing to move or restlessness during times when you’re not in a meeting or event—like when you’re reading, watching TV, or just trying to relax at home?

Not really in a way I can clearly point to, no. I mean, I might shift around at home some, but what brings me in—the part that feels hard to manage—is when I’m supposed to sit still, like in staff meetings or church briefings.

That’s when it feels like there’s this motor humming under my skin, and I end up shifting, standing up if I can, or finding some excuse to move around. At home watching TV or reading, I don’t notice it as much… or maybe it just doesn’t bother anyone, so I don’t think about it. Does that make sense?

Can you tell me about a typical day at home—do you ever find it hard to focus on tasks like reading, watching TV, or following through on something you started, even when there’s no expectation to sit still?

I’m not sure I can give you a clean example there. At home, a typical day is pretty ordinary, and I don’t really notice it the same way.

I mean, if I’m reading or watching TV, I might get up or switch what I’m doing, but I don’t know if that’s more than anyone else would. I don’t want to overstate it. The times that stand out to me are still more the ones where I’m expected to sit still and stay focused.

Does that answer it, or are you looking for something more specific?

When you're at home and trying to do something that requires focus, like reading, following a TV show, or finishing a task around the house, do you ever find yourself getting distracted easily, losing track of what you're doing, or feeling like you need to get up and do something else?

I don’t think I can honestly say I notice that in a big way at home. I mean, sure, I might get up in the middle of a show or put a task down and come back to it, but I’ve never really thought of it as a problem, if that makes sense.

At home there’s no one expecting me to sit there and behave a certain way, so it doesn’t stand out to me as much. The situations where I really notice it are still more when I’m supposed to stay put and pay attention.

I hope that’s answering what you’re asking.

When you're in social situations, like talking with friends or family, do you ever find yourself having trouble focusing, feeling restless, or interrupting others, even when there's no pressure to sit still or look attentive?

A little, yeah… mostly with people who are giving me directions. I don’t mean to be rude or anything, but if my supervisor starts telling me what needs to be done, or someone from the church staff is explaining something, I’ll sometimes jump in before they finish.

It’s like I think I know where they’re going, so I answer too fast. And then sometimes I’m wrong, and they have to correct me or finish what they were trying to say. I’m not trying to cut them off, but I guess it does happen.
Can you think of any time when you felt restless or needed to move when you weren’t in a meeting or church event—like when you’re at home alone, talking with friends, or trying to relax?

Yeah… I guess I do that some. I don’t usually think of it as being “restless,” exactly, because it feels like I’m just keeping busy.

Like on my shifts, I’ll go from mopping to checking the trash to straightening chairs, kind of one thing to the next without really stopping. And even when I get home, instead of just sitting down after work, I might end up puttering around in the garage or re-sorting tools or something like that.

It’s not like I’m trying to avoid relaxing, I don’t think. I just… I tend to stay in motion. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to move around even when you’re at home doing something you enjoy, like watching TV or playing a video game?

Yeah… I mean, not every single time, but yes, I do notice that. Even if I’m watching something I like, I’ll start shifting around or I’ll stand up for a minute, get a drink, check on something, that kind of thing.

It’s almost like there’s a little motor running under my skin when I’m supposed to just sit still. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s honestly a big part of why I brought it up—especially in meetings or church briefings, I feel like I have to move or find some excuse to get up.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
